The test image shows tomato plants in a field collapsing/wilting completely onto raised beds covered with white plastic mulch. Plants remain green but are completely prostrate — no yellowing. This suggests sudden, rapid whole-plant wilt, pointing toward a bacterial wilt disease.

Now let me view one reference image. Given the sudden green wilt pattern, I'll check Bacterial_Wilt.

The reference image shows the bacterial streaming diagnostic test (cut stem in water), confirming the Bacterial_Wilt class context. The test image field view shows the classic field manifestation: sudden, complete whole-plant collapse while leaves remain green — no yellowing, no necrosis, no foliar lesions. This is the hallmark field symptom of Ralstonia solanacearum (bacterial wilt).
